# Tephra

> Tephra is a self-hosted server and web app for Obsidian vaults, with revisioned sync and an MCP endpoint so AI agents can search, read, create and edit notes.

## MCP server

Every Tephra server exposes a Model Context Protocol endpoint at `/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, stateless, JSON responses; MCP protocol versions 2025-06-18, 2025-03-26 and 2024-11-05).

- URL: `https://<your-tephra-host>/mcp` (`POST` only; `GET` returns 405)
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <API token>`. Cookie sessions are not accepted.
- Browser sign-in (recommended): the server implements MCP OAuth 2.1 (authorization code + PKCE, dynamic client registration, loopback redirect). Add the URL to an OAuth-capable agent and authenticate; the agent opens `https://<your-tephra-host>/oauth/authorize`, you sign in and choose a vault and access level, and the agent receives its own API token. Discovery: `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`. Issued tokens (named `MCP: <client>`) can be revoked in the vault's Tokens list.
- Create a token in the web app: open a vault, then Tokens. Scopes: `vault:read-metadata` for search/read, `vault:write` for create/update. A token is bound to one vault, so the `vault` argument is optional.
- Every write is a new vault revision (history is kept). Never put tokens in note contents.

Client config example (Claude Code):

    claude mcp add --transport http tephra https://<your-tephra-host>/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

Generic config:

    { "mcpServers": { "tephra": { "type": "http", "url": "https://<your-tephra-host>/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer <token>" } } } }

### Tools

- `list_vaults` — vaults the token can access. Returns `id`, `name`, `latestRevision`.
- `search_notes` — args: `query` (required), `limit` (1-100, default 20), `vault`. Case-insensitive match on note path and title. Returns `results` with `path`, `fileId`, `blobHash`.
- `read_note` — args: `path` (required, e.g. `Projects/Plan.md`), `vault`. Returns `content`, `blobHash`, `revision`, `size`, `mtime`.
- `create_note` — args: `path` (required, must end in `.md`, canonical vault-relative path, must not already exist case-insensitively), `content` (required), `vault`. Parent folders are implicit.
- `update_note` — args: `path`, `vault`, plus exactly one of:
  - `patch`: a unified diff (`@@ -a,b +c,d @@` hunks; ` ` context, `-` removed, `+` added lines). Context and removed lines must match the current note exactly; line numbers are only hints. `---`/`+++` headers are optional.
  - `content`: the full new note. `baseHash` is then required.
  `baseHash` is the `blobHash` returned by `read_note`; if the note has changed since, the call fails with an edit conflict and you should re-read and retry.

Errors from tools are returned as MCP results with `isError: true` and a message. Authentication failures are HTTP 401.

### Recommended edit flow

1. `search_notes` to find the path, 2. `read_note` to get `content` and `blobHash`, 3. `update_note` with a `patch` (small changes) or `content` + `baseHash` (rewrites).

Example patch for changing line 4 of a note:

    @@ -3,3 +3,3 @@
     one
    -two
    +TWO
     three

## Other docs

- REST API base: `/api/v1` (used by the web app and the Obsidian plugin; same API tokens)
